title: Light in the Study Room
description: Five optical and electrical phenomena are arranged on one desk. Find each setup and select every law that applies.
learning_summary: The study room reveals how light reflects, refracts, forms images, and separates into colors, while electrical energy powers the observations.
learning_points: Light changes direction predictably at reflective and transparent boundaries.
Lenses redirect many rays together to form images with measurable size and position.
White light contains wavelengths that materials can bend by different amounts.
scene_alt: Hand-drawn study room with a desk lamp, mirror, paintbrush in water, magnifying glass, and prism
legend: Find a light or electricity phenomenon

objects.label: Desk lamp
objects.prompt: The lamp converts electrical energy and illuminates the open book. Which processes and laws describe it?
objects.hint: Follow the energy from the electrical circuit to the light and heat produced by the bulb.
objects.explanation: The lamp draws electrical power P = UI and converts electrical energy into light and thermal energy. The total energy remains conserved even though its form changes.
reasoning_steps: Voltage drives current through the lamp's electrical components.
Electrical power measures how quickly the lamp receives energy.
That energy becomes visible light and heat rather than being destroyed.

objects.label: Table mirror
objects.prompt: The upright mirror forms an image of the lamp. Which optical process and law apply?
objects.hint: Compare the angle at which a ray reaches the mirror with the angle at which it leaves.
objects.explanation: The mirror forms a virtual image by reflection. Every ray leaves the surface at the same angle at which it arrived, so θᵢ = θᵣ.
reasoning_steps: Light from the object reaches the smooth mirror surface.
Each ray reflects with an angle equal to its incident angle, measured from the normal.
The reflected rays appear to originate behind the mirror, producing a virtual image.

objects.label: Paintbrush in water
objects.prompt: The paintbrush appears bent where it enters the water. Which process and formulas explain the effect?
objects.hint: Light changes speed and direction when it crosses the boundary between air and water.
objects.explanation: Light from the submerged paintbrush changes speed and direction at the water-air boundary. Snell's law relates the two angles, while n = c/v describes the change in light speed.
reasoning_steps: Light travels at different speeds in water and air.
Crossing the boundary changes the ray direction according to Snell's law.
The eye traces the refracted ray backward, so the submerged section appears displaced.

objects.label: Magnifying glass
objects.prompt: The lens makes a star on the poster appear larger. Which processes and formulas describe this?
objects.hint: A converging lens refracts rays to form an enlarged image. Consider both image distance and image size.
objects.explanation: The convex lens refracts light to form a larger virtual image when the object is inside its focal length. The thin-lens equation locates the image and M = hᵢ/hₒ describes its enlargement.
reasoning_steps: The curved lens surfaces refract incoming rays toward the optical axis.
With the object inside the focal length, emerging rays diverge but appear to meet behind the object.
Image distance and magnification describe where the virtual image appears and how large it looks.

objects.label: Glass prism
objects.prompt: White light leaves the prism as a spectrum. Which optical processes and formulas apply?
objects.hint: The ray changes direction at each surface, and different wavelengths bend by different amounts.
objects.explanation: Light refracts at both prism surfaces. Because the refractive index depends on wavelength, the colors bend by different amounts and separate into a spectrum.
reasoning_steps: White light enters the prism and refracts at the first surface.
Different wavelengths experience slightly different refractive indices.
A second refraction increases the separation, revealing the visible spectrum.
